title: "Stay Home, First Gentleman"
notebook: A Halvekist backbencher told the First Gentleman to stay home. The Herald is running it.
Kolvar did not authorize the remark, but he will not disavow it.
Vyktor: ignore it and the story dies in three days. Retaliation starts a proxy war over my family.

narrative.text: A conservative Halvekist backbencher — not Kolvar, but one of his allies — has made a public statement that is circulating through the press: "The First Gentleman should stay home and let his wife govern. When I want architectural advice, I will hire an architect. When I want political commentary, I will read a politician." The remark is crude. It is also effective — the Herald is running it, and the Standard is running a defense of Jonas. Suddenly, Jonas is a political issue.

I did not authorize that statement. But I will not disavow it either. Your husband has positioned himself as a public figure. Public figures are criticized. That is the arrangement. If Jonas does not want to be attacked by politicians, he should stop acting like one.

The attack is crude but it is also an opportunity. If you defend Jonas publicly — personally, not politically — you remind the public that you are human. If you ignore it, the story dies in three days. If you retaliate, you start a proxy war with the Halvekist caucus over your family. Choose carefully.

choices.text: "The Halvekist backbencher who attacked my husband this morning has forgotten something. Jonas Ashavel is not a politician seeking office. He is a citizen exercising his right to speak. The day this government tells its citizens to stay home and be quiet is the day I resign. That day has not come. And neither has the day when I let bullies in the Assembly chamber dictate what my family is allowed to say."
"I will not dignify that with a response. Jonas does not need me to defend him. He is an adult. If the Halvekists want to waste their time attacking my husband, let them. I have a country to govern."
